Hi Priya / Carlos,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the items we agreed to follow up on so your security and procurement teams can evaluate Redwood for FinCo's chatbot pilots: 

1) Scope & data types
- Primary concern: PII in user messages (names, national IDs) and whether any of that leaves your control.
- We confirmed Redwood's hosted API does not persist full customer request/response payloads by default; telemetry vs. request logging is configurable.

2) Retention & logging controls
- Desired retention for logs: 90 days for basic telemetry; request/response logs must be explicitly enabled and can be configured for redaction/masking or routed to customer-owned storage.
- Access controls: role-based access + audit logs; we can provide attestation and sample audit logs.

3) Data residency & subprocessors
- FinCo needs EU residency for production workloads (eu-west-1 or Azure West Europe).
- Subprocessors discussed: telemetry/monitoring, analytics, cloud provider, marketplace integrations.

4) Action items / next steps
- Jonas: send a short technical note on what telemetry contains vs. request logs, redaction options, and a link to the infra diagram (Jonas to attach subprocessor list).
- Dev (Legal): send DPA draft and SOC 2 attestation copy.
- Marissa: schedule follow-up with FinCo security team next week to validate controls.

Attachments: we will provide a subprocessor list and DPA draft.

Proposed follow-up: Thu 11 Mar, 10:00-10:30am GMT, is that feasible for your security team?

Thanks,

Hi Priya,

Appreciate the questions. Short technical answers below, plus next steps. See attached subprocessor list (redwood_subprocessors_20260309.csv) and architecture diagram at the link Marissa included.

1) Telemetry vs request/response logs
- Telemetry: metrics and aggregated anonymized traces (CPU, latency percentiles, error rates, throughput). No customer message content is included in standard telemetry buckets.
- Request/response logs: optional. When enabled, request/response logs capture raw payloads; we ship these to a configurable sink.

2) Redaction & PII handling
- We support redaction rules at the ingestion point: regex-based masking for emails, phone numbers, national IDs, and configurable removal of user_text fields.
- Redaction is deterministic masking (tokens replaced with fixed tags) and can be applied server-side before storage. If you require irreversible one-way hashing, we can offer a customer-side preprocessor or route logs to your S3 where you control retention and further processing.

3) Data residency
- Production can be pinned to eu-west-1 (AWS) or West Europe (Azure). Backups and most logs remain in-region; certain operational telemetry (anonymized metrics) may be aggregated cross-region for platform health but contains no PII.

4) Deletion & termination
- Standard process: upon contract termination we provide options: (a) immediate data wipe with confirmation within 30 days; (b) archival for agreed period. We will include deletion certificates on request.

Next steps / proposed call
- I attached the subprocessor CSV. I can do a 30-minute technical deep-dive Thu 11 Mar, 11:00-11:30 GMT to demo redaction and the customer-s3 routing pattern. If that works we can invite your platform/security engineer.

Regards,
